title: Lazur vs Claude for Mac in 2026: which one fits your daily work
metaTitle: Lazur vs Claude for Mac: price, privacy and features (2026)
description: Lazur vs Claude for Mac compared on price, privacy, macOS versions and voice features, with sourced prices and where each app is the better pick.
intro: Lazur and Claude for Mac are both AI tools you can call from a Mac, but they do different jobs. Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch. Claude for Mac is Anthropic's desktop app for chatting with Claude, with Quick Entry and paid agent features. Read on for prices, privacy, macOS versions and where each app is the better pick.
tldr: Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant that sees your screen, points at things and answers out loud.
Pick Claude for Mac if you want a full chat app that also runs on Windows, Linux in beta and iOS.
On annual billing, Lazur Pro is $15 a month and Claude Pro is $17 a month. Billed monthly, they are $18 and $20.
Check the macOS version first. Claude's app needs macOS 13 or higher, and its voice dictation needs macOS 14 or later.
Read the training setting. Claude keeps opted-in data for five years and 30 days otherwise. Lazur says content is never used to train AI models.

blocks.text: Lazur and Claude for Mac are both AI tools you can call from a Mac, but they do different jobs. Lazur is a voice assistant that starts from your screen. Claude for Mac starts from a chat window. The sections below show where each one fits, with prices and sources you can check yourself.
What each app does on your Mac

Lazur sits in the notch at the top of your screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option plus Command, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur looks at the screen only while you hold the keys, then answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Claude for Mac is the Claude Desktop app from Anthropic. Its core is a chat window. Quick Entry opens Claude from any app, voice dictation is built in, and Cowork and computer use sit on paid plans. Anthropic offers one universal DMG for macOS. The same app family also runs on Windows, on Linux in beta and on iOS.
Price: Lazur Pro against Claude Pro

Start with the numbers, since they look close. Claude's pricing page lists Free at $0, with limited usage every 5 hours and every week. Pro is $17 per month with annual subscription discount ($200 billed up front), or $20 if billed monthly. Max is $100 per month. Ultra is $200 per month.

Lazur is simpler to read. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power is $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Both plans include unlimited dictation. Lazur also has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts the first time you open the app.

blocks.text: Compare by the work you do, not the sticker price. Claude's pricing page says how fast you reach a limit depends on the model you use, how long your chats are and how large your files are. A long chat with a big file uses more of your plan than a short question. Anthropic also says prices and plans can change at its discretion, so check the pricing page on the day you buy. You can also visit [Lazur pricing](/pricing) for the current Lazur plan details.

ClaudeAI.Guide, an unofficial review site, says agentic sessions use noticeably more of the plan's usage budget. Before you commit to a paid Claude plan, keep a simple log for a week. Write down when you hit a limit and what you were doing at the time.
Voice and screen: how each app listens and looks

Both apps start from a key, so you can call them from anywhere. In Claude, double-tap Option opens Quick Entry by default. To change it, go to Settings > Desktop app and pick Option + Space or a custom shortcut. Older builds show the same setting under Settings > System, under This computer.

Watch for a clash. Lazur uses ⌥ ⌘. Claude's default Quick Entry uses Option alone. Your fingers can mix them up in a hurry. If you run both, move Claude to Option + Space or a custom shortcut, and keep ⌥ ⌘ for Lazur. Quick Entry also needs Claude running, though the app can sit in the background.

Claude's Quick Entry needs Screen recording and Accessibility permissions. Dictation adds Speech recognition. Grant these in System Settings > Privacy & Security. Anthropic's help article says Quick Entry needs macOS 12 or later, and dictation needs macOS 14 or later. A Mac on macOS 13 can use Quick Entry, but not Claude's dictation.

Lazur's voice work reaches past chat. You can set timers, add Apple Reminders, create Calendar events, write notes, control music and volume, open apps and links, search the web and run Shortcuts, all by voice. Claude's Quick Entry is a fast way to reach the chat. Its help article does not list everyday actions like these.

One Claude setting needs a look. Anthropic's Cowork changelog describes two settings keys, quickEntryScreenshotsEnabled and quickEntryFileSharingEnabled. Setting either one to false turns off screenshots or file attachments in Quick Entry and @-mentions. If you work with client files, check these first.
Dictation: hold fn in Lazur or use Claude's voice dictation

Lazur dictates too, but dictation is not its headline. Hold fn and speak. Clean, formatted text appears at the cursor in any app. You also get snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Both Lazur plans include unlimited dictation.

Claude's voice dictation sits inside Quick Entry and needs macOS 14 or later. ClaudeAI.Guide calls the built-in dictation a plus. That review is one author's opinion from daily use on an M-series MacBook. Test dictation on your own text before you rely on it.

blocks.title: Run a short dictation test
blocks.text: Dictate your next few emails in each app. Count the words you fix by hand. Keep the app that needs fewer fixes.
Privacy: what each app keeps and who can train on it

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Lazur says content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did stays on the Mac.

Claude works on a different rule. Anthropic's consumer terms say that when the training setting is on, Anthropic trains new models on data from Free, Pro and Max accounts. That covers new or resumed chats and coding sessions. Anthropic calls it a choice and says you are always in control of the setting. Opted-in data is kept for five years. Data from people who do not opt in keeps the 30-day retention period.

These choices matter because people share more than they expect. Proton, which sells privacy products, surveyed 4,014 current chatbot users in France, Germany, the UK and the US. It found 66% had discussed at least one sensitive topic with a chatbot. Pew Research Center found 71% of U.S. adults think more AI use will make their personal information less secure.
Before a sensitive chat, open Claude's settings and check the training option. With Lazur, decide what sits on screen before you hold ⌥ ⌘, because that is when it looks.
Platforms and macOS versions you need

Claude for Mac needs macOS 13 (Ventura) or higher, according to Anthropic's install article. The same article lists Windows 10 or higher and Linux in beta. Lazur runs on macOS on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur's facts here do not list a minimum macOS version, so check the [Lazur download page](/download) before you install.

items: Claude Quick Entry: macOS 12 or later
Claude voice dictation: macOS 14 or later
Claude computer use on macOS: macOS 14 or later, per the Cowork changelog entry dated 2026-10-01
Lazur: macOS on Apple silicon and Intel, minimum version not listed in its facts

blocks.text: The versions conflict in one place. The install article says macOS 13, while the Cowork changelog says computer use needs macOS 14. A feature can need more than the app does, so plan for the higher number if you want that feature. Check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac.
Agentic work: Cowork, computer use and Lazur's limits

Cowork is where Claude for Mac goes beyond chat. Anthropic's release notes say a Cowork research preview for macOS arrived for Max plans on January 12, 2026. Pro users got it on January 16, 2026. Anthropic made Cowork generally available on macOS and Windows through the Claude Desktop app on April 9, 2026. Computer use came to Pro and Max users on March 23, 2026.

ClaudeAI.Guide describes Cowork's local-file access on paid plans and says agentic sessions use noticeably more usage. It also calls Cowork a research preview. That label predates the April 9 general availability note, so the review may be out of date. Read the release notes before you trust the label.

Lazur takes a narrower path. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, then comes back with a summary and a report. For a task on your screen, ask Lazur to walk you through it. Lazur circles the button, and you press it.

blocks.title: Know the limit
blocks.text: Lazur guides. It does not operate your apps. If you need an agent that works through a multi-step task on its own, Claude's Cowork is the closer fit, and you should budget for its usage.
Where Claude for Mac is the better pick

Claude for Mac wins on reach. It runs on Mac, Windows, Linux in beta and iOS, so one account can follow you across machines. It also has Cowork, computer use for Pro and Max users, and desktop extensions that connect through MCP. Lazur's facts list none of these. If your team uses Windows, Lazur is not an option yet.

Claude is also the stronger tool for long written work. You can hold a full conversation and attach files in the chat. Lazur is built around short voice requests. Reviews of Claude's Mac app are split. ClaudeAI.Guide says Quick Entry 'roughly doubled how often I asked Claude small questions'. John Gruber calls the app a non-native Electron app and argues the reasons for it are weak. Both are opinions, so weigh them against your own tests.
Where Lazur is the better pick

Lazur fits questions about what is on your screen right now. Ask where the export button is, and Lazur circles it with a label. Ask how to change a setting, and it guides you one click at a time. Anthropic's changelog says Quick Entry can include screenshots. The sources for this page do not show Quick Entry pointing at a control on your screen.

Lazur also covers small daily tasks. Timers, Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music, volume, apps, links and web search all run by voice. If your day is full of small errands on the Mac, a voice assistant saves more time than a long chat window. Lazur keeps its memory of what you asked and did on the Mac.

Price is the other reason. On annual billing, Lazur Pro is $15 a month and Claude Pro is $17 a month. Lazur's trial needs no card. Claude's Free plan costs $0, but it limits usage every 5 hours and every week, so heavy daily use runs into the cap.
Mistakes people make when comparing these apps

items: Comparing monthly prices only. Claude Pro is $17 on annual billing and $20 billed monthly. Lazur Pro is $15 billed annually and $18 billed monthly.
Treating Quick Entry as screen help. Quick Entry opens a chat. Lazur points at things and answers out loud.
Expecting Lazur to act for you. It does not click, edit files or operate apps.
Checking only the app minimum. Dictation needs macOS 14, and computer use needs macOS 14 per the changelog.
Skipping the training setting. Opted-in Claude chats keep data for five years. Others keep it for 30 days.
Testing with a short question. Limits depend on the model, chat length and file size, so test with your real work.

blocks.text: How to test both apps in one week

Start with Lazur, because its trial clock starts when you first open the app. Pick a week when you can use the Mac every day. Claude's Free plan has no trial clock, but usage limits apply every 5 hours and every week.

items: Install Lazur from the [Lazur download page](/download) and open it once. The 3-day trial starts here.
Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about a window you use every day, and listen to the spoken answer.
Ask Lazur where a control is. Watch for the circle and the label.
Install Claude for Mac from claude.ai/download. The link redirects to claude.com/download.
Open Settings > Desktop app and pick a Quick access shortcut that does not clash with ⌥ ⌘.
Grant Screen recording and Accessibility in System Settings > Privacy & Security. Add Speech recognition if you want dictation.
Open Claude's settings and check the training option before you paste client or personal text.
Run the same tasks in both apps and note which one you reached for without thinking.

blocks.text: Keep the notes short. Write down the task, the app and the time it took. Over a week, the app you open without thinking tells you more than any table. Pick that one, then check the plan price that fits your use.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Claude for Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. The two apps run separately on your Mac. Lazur's facts do not describe a link to Claude's app, so treat them as separate products.

faq.question: Which is cheaper, Lazur Pro or Claude Pro?
faq.answer: On annual billing, Lazur Pro is $15 a month and Claude Pro is $17 a month with annual subscription discount. Billed monthly, Lazur Pro is $18 and Claude Pro is $20. Check both pricing pages before you buy, because Anthropic says its plans can change.

faq.question: Does Claude for Mac run on macOS 13?
faq.answer: Yes. Anthropic's install article lists macOS 13 (Ventura) or higher for Claude Desktop. Quick Entry needs macOS 12 or later, and voice dictation needs macOS 14 or later.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It points, explains and guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on.

faq.question: Does Claude use my chats for training?
faq.answer: Only if the training setting is on. Anthropic says that setting applies to Free, Pro and Max accounts. If you opt in, data is kept for five years. If you do not, the 30-day retention period applies.

faq.question: Is there a free trial for Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app, so open it on a day you can test it properly.

faq.question: Does Claude for Mac have a free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. The Free plan costs $0 and has limited usage every 5 hours and every week. How fast you reach a limit depends on the model you use, how long your chats are and how large your files are.

faq.question: Which app should I use if my team also has Windows PCs?
faq.answer: Claude's desktop app also runs on Windows. Lazur runs on macOS only for now. Windows is planned, not available, so Lazur does not cover Windows machines yet.

faq.question: Can I run Lazur and Claude's Quick Entry at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes, but change Claude's Quick access shortcut if you want to keep ⌥ ⌘ for Lazur. Claude's default is a double-tap of Option. Option + Space is another choice in Claude's Desktop app settings.

verdict: Pick Lazur if most of your Mac work is small voice tasks and questions about what is on screen. Pick Claude for Mac if you want a full chat app across Mac, Windows, Linux and iOS, or Cowork agent sessions on a paid plan. If you cannot decide, use Lazur's 3-day trial and Claude's Free plan for one week, then keep the app you reached for first.
